chapter: Later albums and the Neville connection
title: Hercules, written for Aaron Neville
summary: Hercules was written for Aaron, recorded partly in Atlanta, and did little commercially.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I forget on which piece. I think it might have been on a thing called Pickle. You've had a little bit, a few piano bars from the beginning of the Hallelujah Chorus. Do you remember that? It's just this... That's a real nice surprise in that. Makes it a lot of fun. A song that's been a mystery to me, I didn't even discover until I was putting together another program, was something you, I think you wrote for Aaron Neville called Hercules. Did you write that and arrange it?
Right. Do you remember who's in the band on that?

I think that was on the session in Atlanta, that we did some in Atlanta and some here. And a couple of Atlanta musicians, not a couple more than that of Atlanta musicians, like Barry Bailey, I think, who's with Atlanta Rhythm Section now.
I would have to go downstairs and look at that and take another look at that.
That's a song I really wish had gone further. Is that one that you thought would? Or it seemed like it was a song that should have gone a lot further than it did.

I don't know. When we were through with it, I listened and it... It sounded like an awful lot of words, but I sort of liked it. It was written especially for Aaron to do. If it wasn't for Aaron, a song like that wouldn't have been written. To say those things. There are a lot of lines in there as the kind of lines that Aaron rapped when he talked. He talked like that. And he inspires a lot of things. Not that that's a different story that I know of, but... I could easily set up a scene from Aaron talk and write songs like that all day long.

I played that song on a show we did with the Neville Brothers about two months ago. And I don't think it's possible to find a copy of that record anywhere in the city now. Because there's such a huge response to it. And when it came out, I never heard it here in New Orleans.

It didn't do much at all. And it was a different sounding record for us. It was a little more... It sounded like a little more percussion. A little more production also. But it didn't do very much, but we liked it.
